note: Deterministic hand-designed golden fixture for the callscore engine. Inputs are committed CSVs; expected outputs are JSON row arrays matching the callscore_core.frames contracts exactly (column names, order, dtypes, sort order). Regenerate with: python3 server/packages/engine/tests/golden/reference.py (stdlib only; never imports callscore_engine/callscore_core).

run_context.note: knowledge_cutoff excludes event e26 (knowledge_ts 2025-05-26T00:00:00Z), which would otherwise correct e11; e11 therefore remains a sell interval in every expected output.

calendar.dst: US DST starts 2025-03-09 inside the range; open/close UTC timestamps shift 14:30Z/21:00Z (EST) to 13:30Z/20:00Z (EDT).

variants.default: Methodology() defaults: next_open, hard_close, sector benchmark, horizons (63,126,252).
variants.decay: expiry_policy=decay, decay_days=5; decay_start_session = first session after the expiry session, exit = close of the 5th session after it.
variants.fixed: fixed_horizons_days=(5,10), primary_fixed_horizon_days=10 so d5/d10 censoring is visible inside 62 sessions.

market_events.split: S2 2:1 split at session index 30 (adj_factor 1->2, raw prices halve).
market_events.dividend: S3 cash_dividend 0.30 at session index 40 (reinvested at that open).
market_events.delisting: S5 bankrupt at session index 45 (last traded session 2025-04-30), final_return=-1.0; row retained, never dropped.
market_events.halt: S4 is_halted sessions index 20..24 (open=close=previous close, tr_index flat).
market_events.missing_benchmark: inputs/benchmark_daily_missing_day.csv is the full benchmark_daily minus SECTOR_TECH on 2025-04-01 (session index 25), a date on which many intervals exit; any run consuming it must fail with MissingBenchmarkData rather than assume zero.

tolerances.tr_index_recursion: recompute tr_index from stored open/close/adj_factor/cash_dividend; |rel err| <= 1e-9

derivation_notes.available_ts: max(effective_ts, knowledge_ts); all events have effective_ts == announced_ts except e26 (invisible).
derivation_notes.entry: next_open: first session open strictly after available_ts on the security's exchange. Announcement times: PRE=12:00Z (same-day open), DAY=15:00Z and POST=21:30Z (next session open), valid across the EST/EDT switch.
derivation_notes.interval_id: equals event_id. Same-canonical actions (e03 reiteration, e07 pt_change) open no interval and extend expiry to the newest non-null expiry; e22/e23 are hidden by the visible 2-deep correction chain e23->e24, so e24 (sell) is the interval-opening event.

exit_reasons.superseded: exit at the next interval's entry point (an open).
exit_reasons.dropped: e05 drop exits e04's interval at the drop's would-be entry point (2025-04-01 open).
exit_reasons.expired: hard_close: close of last session on/before expiry_date; decay: close of session expiry_idx+5 with decay_start_session=expiry_idx+1.
exit_reasons.coverage_ended: e28 exits at close of last session on/before A3's S5 coverage to_date (session index 40).
exit_reasons.analyst_left: A2's employment spell ends session index 50; open A2 intervals exit at its close (e15 under decay, e18 under all policies).
exit_reasons.delisted: e12 exits at S5's delisting session close; terminal value = close level x (1 + final_return) = 0.
exit_reasons.run_end: e30 has null expiry and is the last interval; exits at as_of close 2025-05-23.

derivation_notes.e29_short_interval: e29 announced post-close 2025-03-11 and e30 pre-market 2025-03-12 both get entry 2025-03-12 open, so the sell interval has entry == exit: kept, is_investable=false, non_investable_reason=shorter_than_one_session, exit_reason=superseded.
derivation_notes.non_investable: e09 under_review (suspend) and e17 restricted are intervals with null weight; never treated as hold.
derivation_notes.returns: to_exit plus d63/d126/d252 (default, decay) or d5/d10 (fixed). Fixed d{n} ends at the close of the session n sessions after entry; beyond as_of => unavailable_reason=horizon_incomplete with null legs. Non-investable intervals => unavailable_reason=non_investable. Delisting terminates any horizon reaching it (terminated_by_delisting=true, final_return applied to the terminal close level).
derivation_notes.benchmark: sector mode: SECTOR_<sector> of the security's classification spell at entry_session (S1/S2 TECH, S3/S4 HLTH, S5 FIN).
derivation_notes.contributions: absolute weights strong_buy=1.0, buy=0.5, hold=0.0, sell=-0.5, strong_sell=-1.0. to_exit = weight x to_exit excess for single-segment policies; under decay it is the sum over exposure segments (full weight to expiry close, then w x (1-k/5) per decay session). Fixed horizons use the entry (first-segment) weight.
ambiguities_resolved: Delisted exit_price is reported as the terminal price level close_px x (1+final_return) (0.0 for the bankruptcy), so price-basis and TR-basis legs stay consistent; stock_return = -1.0 exactly.

Unavailable return rows keep start/end session+point populated where the schedule is known (non_investable rows carry the interval's exit point; horizon_incomplete rows have null end_*); entry/exit prices and returns are null.
benchmark_id is populated on every return row, including unavailable ones, because benchmark assignment is interval-level, not leg-level.
decay_start_session is set only for intervals whose binding exit is expired under the decay policy.
flags carries the structural non-investable reason (shorter_than_one_session) when present; canonical-rating reasons (under_review, restricted) are reported via non_investable_reason only.
